root_cause.text: In `drivers/accel/amdxdna/amdxdna_ubuf.c`, `amdxdna_get_ubuf()` accumulated user-provided buffer lengths into `exp_info.size` with plain integer addition, so a large `va_ent[i].len` could overflow the size calculation and lead to an undersized allocation.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces `exp_info.size += va_ent[i].len;` with `check_add_overflow(exp_info.size, va_ent[i].len, &exp_info.size)` and returns `-EINVAL` on overflow, and the CVE states the “ubuf size calculation may overflow, resulting in an undersized allocation and possible memory corruption.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Add the overflow-checking header so the file can use kernel overflow helper APIs.
intent_record.what: A new header include, <linux/overflow.h>, was added alongside the existing DRM and memory-management includes.
intent_record.how: This makes overflow-checking helpers available in the compilation unit, enabling the code to use kernel arithmetic overflow detection macros or functions at runtime/compile time where needed.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add overflow checking when accumulating user buffer size to prevent wraparound and reject invalid large inputs.
intent_record.what: The code replacing a plain addition to exp_info.size now uses check_add_overflow() when adding va_ent[i].len; if overflow is detected, it sets ret to -EINVAL and jumps to free_ent instead of continuing.
intent_record.how: This prevents exp_info.size from wrapping around on large accumulated lengths, which avoids computing an incorrect buffer size and later allocating or mapping memory based on an overflowed value. On overflow, the function now fails early with an invalid-argument error.

candidates.rationale: This plain addition accumulates user-controlled lengths into exp_info.size without overflow checking, so a large va_ent[i].len can wrap the total size and cause an undersized allocation.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement adds a user-controlled length into exp_info.size using plain integer addition. Without overflow checking, the total can wrap around, producing an undersized allocation and enabling the vulnerability described.

commit bd72d4acda1069579b35123e3cc0b21ec1193a21
Author: Lizhi Hou <lizhi.hou@amd.com>
Date:   Wed Jul 16 09:44:14 2025 -0700

    accel/amdxdna: Support user space allocated buffer
    
    Enhance DRM_IOCTL_AMDXDNA_CREATE_BO to accept user space allocated
    buffer pointer. The buffer pages will be pinned in memory. Unless
    the CAP_IPC_LOCK is enabled for the application process, the total
    pinned memory can not beyond rlimit_memlock.
    
    Reviewed-by: Jacek Lawrynowicz <jacek.lawryn
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is present in this function. In the loop it initializes `exp_info.size = 0` and then does plain addition: `exp_info.size += va_ent[i].len;`. Because `va_ent[i].len` is user-controlled, a large value can overflow the accumulated size. The code then derives the allocation/pinning count from that sum with `ubuf->nr_pages = exp_info.size >> PAGE_SHIFT;`, so an overflow here can produce an undersized page count. There is no overflow check or saturation (for example, no `check_add_overflow()` or bounds validation) anywhere in the shown function, so the fix is not present.
